summary:
[  edit  ]
The Noise  TOP  generates a variety of noise patterns including perlin, simplex, sparse, alligator and random. Some types of noise run on the CPU, while others are calculated on the  GPU . The ones that are calculated on the  GPU  will have  GPU  in their name.
The first input can be combined with the generated noise in various ways depending on the parameters.
The second input can be used to specify noise coordinates per-pixel. Without a 2nd input connected, the noise coordinates are the 0-1 texture coordinates of the output texture, i.e, the position of the pixel in the output texture. With a 2nd input connected the position of the pixel in the output texture is used to look-up into the 2nd input, and the RGBA of the 2nd input for that sampled pixel will be used as the XYZ and W for the noise coordinate.
Note:  This  TOP  supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays. For this  TOP  to generate a 3D texture output, it requires a 3D texture type as input. You can use a  Texture 3D TOP  or  GLSL TOP  to create 3D texture types.

inputs.description: Composite Input  - Control the Composite operation via the parameters on the Output Page of this operator.
Noise Coordinate Map  - A texture specifying the 2, 3 or 4 dimensional lookup into the noise field.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.name: type
parameters.description: ⊞  - The noise function used to generate noise. The functions available are:

parameters.label: Perlin 2D ( GPU )
parameters.name: perlin2d
parameters.description: Perlin noise function calculated on the  GPU .  Choose between 2, 3, and 4 dimensional functions.

parameters.label: Perlin 3D ( GPU )
parameters.name: perlin3d
parameters.description: Perlin noise function calculated on the  GPU .  Choose between 2, 3, and 4 dimensional functions.

parameters.label: Perlin 4D ( GPU )
parameters.name: perlin4d
parameters.description: Perlin noise function calculated on the  GPU .  Choose between 2, 3, and 4 dimensional functions.

parameters.label: Simplex 2D ( GPU )
parameters.name: simplex2d
parameters.description: Simplex noise function calculated on the  GPU .  Choose between 2, 3, and 4 dimensional functions.

parameters.label: Simplex 3D ( GPU )
parameters.name: simplex3d
parameters.description: Simplex noise function calculated on the  GPU .  Choose between 2, 3, and 4 dimensional functions.

parameters.label: Simplex 4D ( GPU )
parameters.name: simplex4d
parameters.description: Simplex noise function calculated on the  GPU .  Choose between 2, 3, and 4 dimensional functions.

parameters.label: Random ( GPU )
parameters.name: randomgpu
parameters.description: Every sample is randomly generated, calculated on the  GPU .

parameters.label: Sparse
parameters.name: sparse
parameters.description: Produces high quality, continuous noise based on Sparse Convolution.

parameters.label: Hermite
parameters.name: hermite
parameters.description: Quicker than Sparse, but produces lower quality noise.

parameters.label: Harmomic Summation
parameters.name: harmonic
parameters.description: Sparse noise with the ability to control the frequency step of the harmonics. Slowest type.

parameters.label: Random
parameters.name: random
parameters.description: (White Noise) Every sample is random and unrelated to any other sample. It is the same as "white noise" in audio.

parameters.label: Alligator
parameters.name: alligator
parameters.description: Cell Noise.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Any number, integer or non-integer, which starts the random number generator. Each number gives completely different noise patterns, but with similar characteristics.

parameters.label: Period
parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The approximate separation between peaks of a noise cycle. It is expressed in Units. Increasing the period stretches the noise pattern out.

parameters.label: Harmonics
parameters.name: harmon
parameters.description: The number of higher frequency components to layer on top of the base frequency. The higher this number, the bumpier the noise will be (as long as roughness is not set to zero). 0 harmonics give the base shape.

parameters.label: Harmonic Spread
parameters.name: spread
parameters.description: The factor by which the frequency of the harmonics are increased. It is normally 2. A spread of 3 and a base frequency of 0.1Hz will produce harmonics at 0.3Hz, 0.9Hz, 2.7Hz, etc.. This parameter is only valid for the Harmonic Summation type.

parameters.label: Harmonic Gain
parameters.name: gain
parameters.description: Amount of the Harmonic Gain layered on top of the base frequency.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.name: rough
parameters.description: Controls the effect of the higher frequency noise. When roughness is zero, all harmonics above the base frequency have no effect. At one, all harmonics are equal in amplitude to the base frequency. When roughness is between one and zero, the amplitude of higher harmonics drops off exponentially from the base frequency.

parameters.label: The default roughness is 0.5. This means the amplitude of the first harmonic is 0.5 of the base frequency, the second is 0.25, the third is 0.125. The harmonics are added to the base to give the final shape. The Harmonics parameter and the Roughness parameter must both be non
parameters.description: zero to see the harmonic effects.

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.name: exp
parameters.description: Pushes the noise values toward 0, or +1 and -1. (It raises the value to the power of the exponent.) Exponents greater than one will pull the channel toward zero, and powers less than one will pull peaks towards +1 and -1. It is used to reshape the channels.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.name: amp
parameters.description: Defines the noise value's amplitude (a scale on the values output).

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Defines the midpoint color of the noise pattern, the default is 0.5 grey.

parameters.label: Monochrome
parameters.name: mono
parameters.description: Toggle color or monochrome noise.

parameters.label: Aspect Correct
parameters.name: aspectcorrect
parameters.description: Controls if the noise takes aspect ratio into account when calculating it's noise coordinates. When this is off, the noise will stretch to fit a non-square aspect ratio texture.

parameters.label: The Translate, Rotate, Scale and Pivot parameters let you sample in a different part of the 3D noise space. Imagine a different noise value for every XYZ point in space. Normally, the Noise  CHOP  samples the noise space from (0,0,0) along the X
parameters.description: axis in steps of 2/period. By changing the transform, you are translating, rotating and scaling the plane along which the Noise TOPs samples the noise space. A slight Y-rotation is like walking in a straight path in the mountains, recording your altitude along the way, then re-starting from the same initial location, walking in a slightly different direction. Your altitude starts off being similar but then diverges.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - The menu attached to this parameter allows you to specify the order in which the transforms will take place. Changing the Transform order will change where things go much the same way as going a block and turning east gets you to a different place than turning east and then going a block.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - The rotational matrix presented when you click on this option allows you to set the transform order for the rotations. As with transform order (above), changing the order in which the rotations take place will alter the final position.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - Translate the sampling plane through the noise space.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - Rotate the sampling plane in the noise space.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - Scale the sampling plane.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - Control the pivot for the transform of the sampling plane.

parameters.label: Translate 4D
parameters.name: t4d
parameters.description: When doing 4D noise, this applies a translation to the 4th coordinate. The previous transformation parameters do not affect the 4th coordinate.

parameters.label: Scale 4D
parameters.name: s4d
parameters.description: When doing 4D noise, this applies a scale to the 4th coordinate.

parameters.label: RGB
parameters.name: rgb
parameters.description: ⊞  - When an input is connected to the Noise  TOP , the noise pattern is placed over the input image using UV coordinates and the settings from this menu.

parameters.label: Noise
parameters.name: noise
parameters.description: Just the noise is output.

parameters.label: Input * Noise
parameters.name: multiply
parameters.description: The noise is multiplied with the input.

parameters.label: Input + Noise
parameters.name: add
parameters.description: The input is added to the noise.

parameters.label: Input - Noise
parameters.name: subtract
parameters.description: The input is subtracted from the noise.

parameters.label: Input Scale
parameters.name: inputscale
parameters.description: Adjusts how much of the input image is added to the output.

parameters.label: Noise Scale
parameters.name: noisescale
parameters.description: Adjusts how much of the noise is added to the output.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the alpha channel for the output image.

parameters.label: Zero
parameters.name: zero
parameters.description: Alpha channel is zero.

parameters.label: One
parameters.name: one
parameters.description: Alpha channel is one.

parameters.label: Noise
parameters.name: random
parameters.description: Alpha channel is random noise.

parameters.label: Input
parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Alpha is the pass through from the input.

parameters.label: Input * Noise
parameters.name: multiply
parameters.description: Alpha is the result of the input's alpha channel * the noise.

parameters.label: Input + Noise
parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Alpha is the result of the input's alpha channel + the noise.

parameters.label: Input + clamp(Noise)
parameters.name: addclamp
parameters.description: Alpha is the result of the input's alpha channel + the noise but clamped around [0-1].

parameters.label: Dither
parameters.name: dither
parameters.description: Dithers the output to help deal with banding and other artifacts created by precision limitations of 8-bit displays.

parameters.label: Gradient
parameters.name: gradient
parameters.description: Turn this on to output the gradient (also known as slope) of the noise function. Currently, only supported for Performance mode Simplex and Perlin noise types. For 2D noise derivatives, the RG channels get populated with the XY derivatives. For 3D, the RGB channels get populated with the XYZ derivatives. And for 4D, the RGBA channels get populated with XYZW derivatives. Note that this calculates derivative of the noise function not derivatives along the noise image.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Pick between Performance vs Quality noise. Performance noise is the existing TD noise. Quality noise reduces certain artifacts and axis alignment issues with the existing noise at the cost of speed. Currently only enabled for Simplex Noise type.

parameters.label: Performance
parameters.name: performance
parameters.description: Performant noise.

parameters.label: Quality
parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: Quality noise.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect

parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input

parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .
